# CSCO — Quantitative Fundamental-Attractiveness Report
**Decision Date: 2026-05-15 | Latest Filing: 2026-01-24 (Q2 FY26)**

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings & Margin Trajectory

Cisco is posting accelerating top-line growth. Quarterly revenue rose from $13.99B (2025-01-25 Q2) to $15.35B (2026-01-24 Q2), delivering **+9.7% YoY** and **+3.1% QoQ**. The trajectory is monotonic across all four available quarters: $13.99B → $14.15B → $14.88B → $15.35B.

EPS growth outpaces revenue, climbing from $0.61 to $0.80 over the same YoY span (**+31.1% YoY**, +11.1% QoQ). This operating leverage reflects genuine margin expansion, not just revenue flow-through:

- **Gross margin** has been remarkably stable: 65.1% → 65.6% → 65.5% → 64.9% (Q2 FY26). The latest quarter shows a slight dip but remains in a tight channel.
- **Operating margin** expanded materially: 22.2% → 22.6% → 22.6% → **24.6%** in the latest quarter — a meaningful step-up.
- **Net margin** followed suit: 17.4% → 17.6% → 19.2% → **20.6%**.

ROE has improved from 20.2% (May 2025) to **23.2%** (latest ratio), confirming that returns on equity are genuinely rising, not just being inflated by leverage.

## 2. Cash Flow & Balance-Sheet Resilience

**Cash generation is a concern.** Operating cash flow was $2.24B → $4.06B → $3.21B → **$1.82B** in the latest quarter — a **QoQ decline of -43.3%** and YoY of -18.7%. This occurred despite rising revenue and net income, suggesting working-capital deterioration (likely receivables or deferred revenue timing). Free cash flow is unavailable, so OCF is the primary cash-generation read. The gap between reported net income ($3.17B) and OCF ($1.82B) — a $1.35B shortfall — flags potential earnings-quality questions that require further filing inspection.

The balance sheet remains solid. Total equity grew steadily: $45.53B → $45.94B → $46.87B → **$47.72B**. Total debt is stable at **$24.60B** (unchanged QoQ, up from $20.10B a year ago). Debt-to-equity of **0.515** is moderate for a tech infrastructure firm. Total assets of $123.37B provide a wide cushion. There is no balance-sheet fragility here.

## 3. Valuation vs. Own History

This is where the quantitative case weakens sharply. On 2026-05-14, the trailing PE stands at **41.56x** — the absolute ceiling of its 365-day range (25.8–41.6). One year ago (2025-05-15), the same PE was **28.01x**. That is a **+49% multiple expansion** over a period when diluted EPS grew ~31%.

P/B has expanded even more aggressively: from **5.65x** (May 2025) to **9.65x** (May 2026), also at the top of its 5.5–9.6 range — a **71% expansion**.

The earnings yield of **2.4%** now sits far below the 10-year Treasury yield of **4.47%**, creating a **-207 bps negative spread**. In a 4.47% risk-free environment, paying 41.6x for a company growing EPS at 31% requires that growth rate to be sustained or accelerated. Any deceleration compresses the thesis quickly. The stock is priced for continued double-digit earnings growth and stable-to-expanding multiples — a high bar.

P/S of 7.79x is likewise elevated for a hardware/networking incumbent.

## 4. Price Context vs. Fundamentals

Price has surged **+54.0%** in the latest ~63-day quarter (from $75.00 on 2026-02-12 to $115.53 on 2026-05-14), after two quarters of modest gains (+1.9%, +4.6%). The stock sits just 3.2% below its 365-day high of $119.36. The price move has dramatically outpaced the underlying earnings improvement — the quarterly earnings growth of ~11% QoQ vs. a 54% price surge means virtually all the re-rating is multiple expansion, not fundamental catch-up.

## 5. Macro & Sentiment Overlays

**Macro is a headwind for the valuation thesis.** The 10-year Treasury has climbed from 4.05% to 4.47% (+42 bps) over the period, while the 2-year surged from 3.43% to 4.00% (+57 bps). The 10Y-2Y spread has compressed to **0.47%**, signaling a flattening curve. Rising long rates directly compress the justified PE for long-duration cash-flow streams — and at 41.6x, CSCO is firmly in that bucket.

WTI crude has spiked +67% to $104.66/bbl — a potential indirect cost and macro-growth risk, though not directly relevant to Cisco's networking business.

VIX has normalized to **17.26** from 31+ in late March, supporting risk appetite, which may partly explain the aggressive re-rating. Breakeven inflation at 2.47% is creeping higher.

**News sentiment** is moderately positive (mean = 0.433 over 49 articles), with the latest day (2026-05-14) showing a perfect 1.0 score across 8 articles. This is the weakest signal in the pack and does not override valuation concerns.

## 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside & Downside

**Upside:** If the Q2 FY26 operating-margin step-up to 24.6% proves durable (vs. the ~22.5% run-rate of prior quarters), and revenue sustains ~10% YoY growth, the earnings trajectory could justify a mid-30s PE — implying still-reasonable appreciation if the market rewards a higher-quality earnings stream. The improving ROE (23.2%) and expanding net margins (20.6%) are real and underappreciated if sustained.

**Downside:** The OCF-to-net-income divergence (OCF $1.82B vs. NI $3.17B) is the single biggest red flag. If this gap persists, it undermines the quality of the earnings beat. Combined with the PE at a 365-day extreme, a mean-reversion to even the mid-range (~32x) on the same earnings would imply a ~23% drawdown. Rising rates further compress the justified multiple, creating a double headwind.

## 7. Provisional Conclusion

Cisco's business trajectory is genuinely positive: accelerating revenue, expanding margins, and improving returns on equity. However, the stock has re-rated so aggressively — PE from 28x to 41.6x, P/B from 5.65x to 9.65x — that it now prices in near-perfection at precisely the moment operating cash flow has weakened. The earnings yield (2.4%) trades well below the risk-free rate (4.47%), which is historically unusual for a mature infrastructure company. **Fundamentally attractive business; quantitatively unattractive entry point.** The growth is real, but the market has already paid for it — and then some.

# Cisco Systems (CSCO) — Qualitative Franchise Assessment
**Decision Date: 2026-05-15 | Evidence window: ≤ 2026-05-14**

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Cisco remains the dominant enterprise networking franchise globally, holding approximately 43% of global Ethernet switching revenue and nearly 60% of enterprise routing revenue as of FY2025 (matrixbcg.com, 2026-04-16). It serves 98–99% of the Fortune 500 across 150+ countries. This is a deeply entrenched, scale-driven position with high switching costs in campus, branch, and data center environments.

The franchise narrative has shifted materially since the $28B Splunk acquisition closed in March 2024. Security revenue surged 59.5% YoY to $8.09B in FY2025, making it the fastest-growing segment and the largest single-year dollar increase in company history (quantumrun.com, 2026-05-06). Networking's share of total revenue fell from 60.7% in FY2023 to 50.0% in FY2025, while services grew to 26.6% of revenue — a deliberate mix shift toward recurring, higher-margin streams. Gross margin expanded 2.3pp to 65.0% over the same period, with services gross margin at 68.5% versus product at 63.7%.

R&D investment hit a record $9.3B in FY2025, up 16.5% YoY and representing 16.4% of revenue — the highest R&D intensity in recent company history. This signals genuine reinvestment in the platform, not just financial engineering.

The company generates substantial cash: operating cash flow exceeds $15B annually per management commentary, and Trefis data (2026-04-16) shows CFO/Revenue of ~24% and FCF/Revenue of ~22% on an LTM basis. Capital return is material — $9B+ returned YTD through Q3 FY2026 via dividends and buybacks, with $9.6B remaining under the repurchase authorization (Yahoo Finance earnings call, Q3 FY2026). The dividend yield sits at approximately 2.9%, with 14 consecutive annual increases.

**Franchise quality: High.** The installed base, channel relationships, integrated platform breadth, and recurring revenue transition underpin a durable competitive moat — though with meaningful caveats discussed below.

---

## 2. Recent Developments (Dated)

**Q3 FY2026 Earnings (reported 2026-05-13/14)** — This was a blowout quarter that materially reframed the AI narrative:

- Revenue of $15.84B, up 12% YoY, beating the $15.56B consensus (CNBC, 2026-05-14; Benzinga, 2026-05-14).
- Product orders surged 35% YoY; networking product orders accelerated to more than 50% YoY (investor.cisco.com, Q3 FY2026).
- AI infrastructure orders reached $5.3B YTD; management raised the FY2026 AI order expectation to $9B, up from $5B, and raised expected AI infrastructure revenue to $4B from $3B (investor.cisco.com; CNBC, 2026-05-14).
- GAAP EPS of $0.85 (+37% YoY); non-GAAP EPS of $1.06 (+10% YoY), beating the $1.04 consensus.
- Full-year FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $62.8B–$63.0B.
- Q4 FY2026 guidance of $16.7B–$16.9B revenue with non-GAAP EPS of $1.16–$1.18, well above consensus.

**Restructuring announcement (2026-05-14):** Cisco is cutting fewer than 4,000 jobs (<5% of headcount) with a $1B pre-tax charge (~$450M in Q4, remainder in FY2027), reallocating resources toward silicon, optics, security, and AI (CNBC, 2026-05-14; investor.cisco.com). This is being read as capital reallocation toward growth, not retrenchment.

**Campus networking refresh cycle:** Campus networking orders grew more than 25% YoY, with the next-generation portfolio ramping faster than prior launches. Data center switching orders grew more than 40% YoY (investor.cisco.com, Q3 FY2026).

**Stock reaction:** Shares surged 13–18% on May 14, hitting a 52-week high (Motley Fool, Benzinga, 2026-05-14). The stock has gained approximately 40% over the past month.

---

## 3. Material Risks and Offsets

**Margin compression — the central near-term risk.** Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 66.0% in Q3 FY2026 from 68.6% a year earlier, driven by memory cost pressure and tariff impact. Q4 guidance of 65.5%–66.5% suggests this is persistent, not transitory (business-news-today.com, 2026-05-14; Investing.com, 2026-05-14). If tariff escalation continues, margin pressure into FY2027 could constrain earnings power.

**Security segment stagnation.** Security revenue was flat at ~$2B in Q3 FY2026 despite the Splunk investment. If the security and observability stack does not reaccelerate, Cisco risks being repriced as a cyclical AI hardware beneficiary rather than a structurally diversified platform company (business-news-today.com, 2026-05-14). CEO Chuck Robbins pointed to Q4 Splunk reacceleration, which now carries elevated scrutiny.

**Competition intensifying.** Arista Networks holds nearly 30% of high-speed (100G–800G) switching and posts significantly faster growth (28.6% revenue growth vs. Cisco's ~5%) with superior operating margins (42.8% vs. Cisco's ~20.8%) (matrixbcg.com, 2026-04-16; strategy.transforml.co, 2026-04-16). HPE+Juniper targets AI-native networking. Palo Alto, Fortinet, and CrowdStrike pressure the security portfolio. White-box vendors and hyperscaler vertical integration remain structural threats in data center switching.

**Geopolitical and tariff exposure.** Tariff impacts are embedded in current guidance, but escalation represents an unmodeled downside. The 59% Americas revenue concentration creates concentrated policy exposure (quantumrun.com, 2026-05-06). Export controls and "rip and replace" mandates in sensitive markets add regulatory risk.

**Hyperscaler concentration in AI orders.** The AI order trajectory is impressive but concentrated among a small number of hyperscaler customers. Total product orders excluding hyperscalers grew 19% — solid, but meaningfully below the 35% headline (investor.cisco.com). If hyperscaler capex cycles decelerate, the AI revenue bridge narrows quickly.

**Services revenue decline.** Services revenue was down 1% in Q3 and flat YTD, which is a modest negative signal for the recurring revenue thesis. Management attributed this to contract timing, but it warrants monitoring.

**Offset — diversification and trust.** Cisco's breadth across networking, security, observability, and collaboration, combined with deep enterprise relationships and a channel-centric model, provides resilience against single-segment shocks. The subscription software transition, while incomplete, is directionally positive for revenue quality.

---

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Positive.** The Q3 FY2026 print is the strongest evidence yet that Cisco's AI infrastructure positioning is translating into real orders at scale — not just narrative. The $9B AI order trajectory, 35% total order growth, accelerating networking demand, and a multi-year campus refresh cycle all point to a franchise that is being re-rated on genuinely improved fundamentals, not just momentum. The restructuring signals management discipline in reallocating toward high-growth vectors. The Splunk integration, while slower in security, is building the foundation for a unified networking-security-observability platform that few competitors can replicate at enterprise scale.

**Negative.** Gross margin compression from tariffs and memory costs is real and persistent, threatening to cap earnings leverage even as revenue accelerates. The security segment's flat performance is conspicuous weakness that undermines the platform diversification thesis. Competition from Arista in data center, Palo Alto in security, and white-box vendors in hyperscale remains a genuine structural headwind. Valuation has expanded significantly after the post-earnings surge.

**Net read: Positive.** The franchise quality is high and improving; the AI order momentum and campus refresh create a multi-quarter growth tailwind; and management is actively reallocating resources. However, margin headwinds and security stagnation introduce meaningful execution risk that could limit upside if the AI hardware cycle normalizes. The narrative supports fundamental attractiveness on the strength of the networking franchise and AI positioning, tempered by margin and diversification concerns.

---
